slides.title: Top Use Cases, Structured As Business Jobs
slides.objective: Translate clusters into business jobs, buyers, and value propositions.

content_blocks.label: workflow automation
content_blocks.body: Buyer: COO, operations leader, or workflow owner | Job: Turn high-volume, rules-heavy operational queues into agent-run systems of action. | Value: Throughput, faster cycle times, and lower labor cost without requiring users to learn a new interface. | Why now: LLMs plus tool use make it possible to automate the whole queue, not just summarize it.

content_blocks.label: sales and customer ops
content_blocks.body: Buyer: sales leaders, revenue ops, customer success, or service managers | Job: Use agents to qualify, route, support, and operationalize customer interaction workflows. | Value: Improves responsiveness and rep leverage while keeping the workflow anchored in revenue teams. | Why now: Customer conversations already create structured data and clear SLAs, which agents can exploit.

content_blocks.label: analytics and reporting
content_blocks.body: Buyer: heads of analytics, operations leaders, and knowledge-work teams | Job: Turn raw data or context into dashboards, summaries, and decision-ready reporting. | Value: Makes information work faster and cheaper while reducing manual synthesis. | Why now: Reporting is repetitive, high-frequency, and already evaluated on output quality and speed.

content_blocks.label: developer tools and testing
content_blocks.body: Buyer: engineering leaders, product teams, QA, and platform teams | Job: Use agents to test, monitor, and validate software and model-driven systems. | Value: Catches regressions and scales QA capacity without linearly scaling headcount. | Why now: Agentic products create new failure modes, so testing and observability have become first-order needs.

content_blocks.label: data and agent infrastructure
content_blocks.body: Buyer: platform engineering, CTO staff, and teams building agent products | Job: Provide the data, context, and permissioning layer that agent products depend on. | Value: Becomes infrastructure rather than a single workflow app, increasing platform stickiness. | Why now: Agents fail without trustworthy context and controlled system access.

slides.title: What A Stronger Sync2 Wedge Looks Like
slides.objective: Translate the case-study insight into explicit action.

content_blocks.body: Own a workflow chain like intake -> scheduling -> billing -> claims instead of a single chat entry point.

content_blocks.body: Use operational integration as the moat: EHR, claims, pharmacy, lab, and payer connectivity.

content_blocks.label: Action 3
content_blocks.body: Sell around measurable staffing relief, collection lift, and cycle-time compression.

content_blocks.body: Position as system-of-action software for clinic operations, not as another AI front desk.
